blocks.text:
The next 4 days have no compulsory transfers or excursions.

At Nannai Muro Alto, you can head to the beach in the morning, wait for low tide and swim in the sheltered water behind the reef. There are hardly any strong waves here, the water is warm, and the pale seabed is clearly visible even farther from shore.

For a change of scene, the resort centre offers trips to the natural pools on **jangadas**, the local flat rafts. At low tide, pockets of clear water remain between the reefs, with small fish that are easy to watch with a snorkelling mask.

Diving and buggy rides along the coast are also available.

You can also spend the days without any extra outings: relax by the pool, walk around Muro Alto and return to the sea in the morning and evening, when the sand is cooler. After the busy programme in Rio, Iguaçu and Bonito, this part of the journey offers a few quiet days without constantly changing hotels.
